evidence: backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/listings.rs:432 — the LIVE public listing-detail handler get_listing() (route wired at routes/listings.rs:62 `.route("/{id}", get(get_listing))` and registered in main.rs:150 for `GET /api/v1/listings/{id}`) builds its `ListingDetail` response with `view_count: 0, // Would need analytics query`. Every other field on this response is correctly hydrated from the DB row `l.` (bathrooms, floor, total_floors, latitude, longitude, features, country), so the endpoint is otherwise complete — only the view counter is a hardcoded literal.

The write path for view analytics IS implemented and runs on this very handler: routes/listings.rs:380 calls `state.reality_portal_repo.track_view(id, "website").await` on each detail fetch, and a dedicated `POST /api/v1/listings/{id}/view` (routes/listings.rs:851-870) also increments. Per handlers/listings/mod.rs:127-131 track_view routes through the SECURITY DEFINER `portal_track_listing_view` fn (migration 00214) and lands rows in `listing_analytics`. So views are persisted but the read path was never wired — the response `view_count` is a constant 0.

Net user-facing effect: the public listing page (reality-web + mobile-native KMP) permanently displays 0 views for every listing regardless of real traffic, and any realtor/analytics surface reading this field under-reports to zero. This is a live read-path gap on the core public surface (distinct from the 2026-08-05 incomplete-feature findings). Fix: replace the literal with a `SELECT`/aggregate over `listing_analytics` for the listing id (or a cached counter), mirroring the write path already in place.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/handlers/listings/mod.rs:74-113 — `ListingHandler::get_listing()` returns a `PublicListingDetail` with a whole block of fields hardcoded to empty/false regardless of the DB: `is_negotiable: false`, `bathrooms: None`, `floor: None`, `total_floors: None`, `street: String::new()`, `postal_code: String::new()`, `country: String::new()`, `latitude: None`, `longitude: None`, `features: vec![]` (each carrying a `// Would need to be fetched from DB` comment). A parallel struct, the LIVE `routes/listings.rs::get_listing` (line 411-433), proves those same attributes DO exist on the row (it hydrates `l.bathrooms`, `l.latitude`, `l.country`, etc.) — so this is a stubbing bug, not a missing schema.

However, this handler is dead/orphaned code: a segment-wide grep for `ListingHandler` / `handlers::listings::` / `.get_listing(` call sites finds only the definition in handlers/listings/mod.rs itself — nothing constructs `ListingHandler` or calls this `get_listing()`, and no Axum route is wired to it (the live `GET /api/v1/listings/{id}` uses routes::listings::get_listing per main.rs:150). So there is no current user-facing impact.

Risk is latent-trap + maintenance debt: a future refactor that rewires the public detail route to this handler (a natural-looking choice given its name) would silently ship listings with blank address, no map coordinates (lat/lng None), and empty features. Fix: either delete the orphaned handler, or complete it to hydrate from the same row source routes/listings.rs already uses, so the two detail paths cannot diverge.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/handlers/inquiries/mod.rs:290-337 — `schedule_viewing()` runs full input validation (future-date at :300, <=90-days window at :308, 15-120min duration at :317) and then, at the point it must persist the viewing, unconditionally returns `ViewingResult::ValidationFailed(vec![ValidationError { field: "viewing", message: "Viewing scheduling not yet implemented" }])` (:333-336) after only a `tracing::info!(... "Viewing scheduling requested")`. It creates no record. Reporting a not-implemented feature as a field-level *validation* error is also a semantically wrong contract (should be 501/NOT_IMPLEMENTED, not a 400-shaped validation failure).

Like the listings stub, this method is dead/orphaned: the live viewing route `POST /api/v1/inquiries/viewing/{listing_id}` (routes/inquiries.rs:62 -> request_viewing at :298) does NOT call schedule_viewing — it builds a message embedding the preferred times (routes/inquiries.rs:352-364) and creates a normal inquiry via InquiriesHandler::validate_contact + create. A grep for `schedule_viewing(` call sites finds only its own definition. So the live viewing-request flow works; this handler is unreachable.

Impact is dead-code / incomplete-stub hygiene, not a live outage. Fix: delete schedule_viewing (the real flow lives in request_viewing), or if a structured viewing-record feature is intended, implement the repo write and return a proper success/501 rather than a misleading ValidationFailed. Distinct from the 2026-08-05 inquiry-detail-empty-messages finding.
